key_insight: Singular-value spectra of equivariant representations provide orientation-invariant fingerprints for identifying structural symmetry and quantifying symmetry breaking.
engineering_relevance: SymFP could support symmetry-aware analysis of crystals, molecules and complex assemblies, including local changes that global geometric measures may miss.
method: Extract singular-value spectra from equivariant representations, including a parameter-free GNN implementation.
Identify discrete point groups by matching spectral ranks to symmetry templates.
Quantify symmetry breaking through spectral energy beyond target rank constraints, reusing spectra across target groups.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate point-group identification and tracking of controlled, local and degree-resolved symmetry changes across synthetic structures, molecules, coordination complexes and large biological assemblies.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify numerical rank thresholds or robustness to measurement noise, both important for practical deployment.
paper_title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
